content.value_statement: React and Next.js apps often slow down from waterfalls, heavy bundles, and repeated rendering. This skill gives practical Vercel-style rules for faster frontend code reviews and refactors.
actual_capabilities: Identifies async waterfalls and suggests parallel data fetching patterns.
Recommends bundle-size improvements such as direct imports and dynamic loading.
Guides Server Component data boundaries, caching, and non-blocking server work.
Reviews client-side fetching patterns for SWR deduplication and shared subscriptions.
Suggests re-render and JavaScript performance improvements with focused examples.
Maps performance rules to separate markdown files for deeper agent review.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not automated profiling or benchmark results.
It does not replace application-specific measurement with browser or server tools.
Some recommendations depend on the React, Next.js, and bundler versions in use.
It does not include runnable source code for modifying an application directly.

use_cases.title: Review a Next.js Pull Request
use_cases.description: Find data-fetching waterfalls, excessive client props, and bundle risks before merging a feature.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Slow Product Page
use_cases.description: Apply Suspense boundaries, dynamic imports, and server-side caching to improve perceived performance.

use_cases.title: Teach Performance Patterns
use_cases.description: Use clear incorrect and correct examples to explain React optimization tradeoffs to a team.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic React Performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small component or page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React or Next.js code for obvious performance issues. Focus on waterfalls, unnecessary state reads, and avoidable re-renders.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Bundle Loading
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of imports and third-party libraries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Next.js route for bundle-size problems. Suggest direct imports, dynamic imports, and deferred third-party loading where useful.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Server Data Fetching
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of Server Components or route handlers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this server-side React or Next.js flow to avoid waterfalls. Preserve behavior while starting independent work as early as possible.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Performance Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced end-to-end audit across a feature area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized performance audit plan for this React and Next.js feature. Include expected impact, implementation risk, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: A page fetches user data, configuration, posts, and comments in sequence before rendering.
output: Flags the sequential awaits as a high-impact waterfall.
Recommends starting independent requests together and awaiting dependent data only when needed.
Suggests a Suspense boundary if only part of the page needs the slow data.

output_examples.input: A dashboard imports a large editor and analytics package in the initial route.
output: Recommends loading analytics after hydration and loading the editor only when opened.
Adds an intent-based preload suggestion for hover or focus.

output_examples.input: A client component receives a large user object but displays only the user name.
output: Flags excessive serialization across the server and client boundary.
Recommends passing only the fields the client component uses.
Notes that smaller serialized payloads improve page weight and navigation speed.

best_practices: Measure the feature first, then apply the highest-impact rule that matches the bottleneck.
Keep refactors small and verify behavior with tests, profiling, or production metrics.
Prefer project conventions and framework-supported APIs before adding new abstractions.
anti_patterns: Applying every rule mechanically without checking the current performance bottleneck.
Adding memoization or caching that makes the code harder to maintain without clear benefit.
Moving code to the client when the data or rendering work can remain on the server.

faq.question: Does this skill run performance tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and refactoring patterns. Use profiling tools to confirm measured improvements.

faq.question: Can it help with both React and Next.js?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers general React rendering patterns and Next.js-specific server, routing, and bundle practices.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for reviews and refactors where existing code already shows performance symptoms.

faq.question: Does it require Vercel hosting?
faq.answer: No. Many rules apply to any React or Next.js deployment, though some examples mention Vercel features.

faq.question: Will it change application code by itself?
faq.answer: No. An agent can use the guidance to propose or implement changes when the user asks for edits.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
